page: Microsoft Azure DC32as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DCasv6 family, hosted on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD x86_64 processor architecture and provides 32 dedicated vCPUs paired with 128 GB of system RAM. Utilizing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory distribution, each virtual core receives 4.0 GB of memory, delivering a standard resource envelope for non-specialized cloud computing environments.

The physical configuration of the DC32as_v6 excludes local instance storage entirely. All operating system and workload storage operations require remote disk attachments, with native support for Azure Premium Storage. The machine does not include graphic accelerators or dedicated GPUs, focusing exclusively on CPU execution. Additionally, the configuration comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring virtual network routing or independently provisioned public endpoints for external ingress and egress.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, omitting bundled local disks prevents spending on unused hardware capacity in stateless architectures or designs utilizing decoupled block storage. Furthermore, dedicated core assignments eliminate noisy-neighbor issues at the hypervisor level. This server profile is technically configured for enterprise web services, relational database hosting, container orchestration nodes, and continuous integration pipelines.
description: The Microsoft Azure DC32as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Powered by AMD x86_64 processors, this instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs paired with 128 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local instance storage, instead requiring network-attached remote storage solutions and offering compatibility with Azure Premium Storage. Network interfaces omit complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating configured virtual network gateways or allocated public IPs for external routing. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent computational performance without multi-tenant vCPU contention. Balancing compute and memory resources evenly without the overhead of unused onboard disks, the DC32as_v6 offers a predictable resource configuration. This hardware profile aligns well with enterprise applications, mid-sized relational database management systems, application servers, continuous integration pipelines, and general business workloads.
